summary: Removes the slot addressed by index a2 from a texture/render allocation pool. Validates the active count at this+0x30 and the capacity at this+0x2C, computes the 128-byte slot from the base at this+0x34, and requires the slot's in-use bit (0x40). Two removal paths are selected by the sign of the flags byte at this+0x20: a doubly-linked-list unlink path (prev/next links at slot+120 and slot+124, free-list head at this+0x38) and an array path that swaps the last slot's data into the freed position via a 16-dword copy over the buffer at *(*(this+0x50)+0x20) and fixes the index array at this+0x3C. Both paths clear the in-use bit and decrement the count.

local_names.this: allocation-pool object: flags 0x20, iteration count 0x24, capacity 0x2C, active count 0x30, slot base 0x34, free-list head 0x38, index array 0x3C, sub-context 0x50
local_names.result: active count; early paths return it unchanged, success paths return the decremented count
local_names.v6: iteration count from this+0x24 used by the 16-dword copy loop
local_names.v7: destination dword pointer for the copy into the freed slot
local_names.v8: source dword pointer for the copy from the last slot
local_names.v9: slot's next link used by the list-unlink path

operations.description: If the active count *(this+0x30) is <= 0, return it (empty pool)
If the requested index a2 >= capacity *(this+0x2C), return the count (out of range)
v4 = *(this+0x34) + (a2 << 7) computes the slot pointer from the base at this+0x34 with a 128-byte stride
If the slot's in-use bit (0x40) is clear, return the count (slot already free)
Branch on the signed flags byte at this+0x20: a value >= 0 selects the doubly-linked-list unlink path, otherwise the array/copy path

List path: unlink the slot from the doubly-linked list using the prev link at slot+120 (0x78) and the next link at slot+124; when the slot was the head (no prev), the free-list head at this+0x38 advances to the slot's next link; both links are then zeroed
Array path: if the last slot's pointer in the index array *(*(this+0x3C) + 4*count - 4) is already v4, fall through to the common cleanup (no data move needed)
Array path: TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(0) is invoked before the data-copy step

Array path: copy the last slot's data into the freed slot's position: the sub-context pointer at this+0x50 is dereferenced and +0x20 (0x20) yields the copy buffer v5, dest/source pointers are derived from the slots' ids with a stride of v6 = *(this+0x24), and a loop copies 16 dwords (indexes 0, 1, 2, 6) per iteration while advancing by 16 dwords
Array path: fix the index array at this+0x3C so the freed slot's id maps to the last slot's slot pointer and vice versa
Common cleanup: clear the in-use bit on the slot (*(DWORD*)v4 &= ~0x40) and decrement the active count at this+0x30
Return the old count on the early-return guard paths, or the decremented count on a successful removal
Invoked from sub_4CB5E0 as a slot-deallocation helper

unresolved: Whether this+0x20's flags byte selects two genuinely different slot representations (doubly-linked list vs compact array) or two container modes of one pool is DERIVED from structure, not confirmed.

The purpose of the TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(0) call on the array path (allocation with a zero format argument before copying) is unresolved; it may guarantee a backing buffer for the copy.
The exact meaning of the slot dword at +4 is only partially resolved: it serves as the copy-stride index and as the value stored into the index array.

The packet's field base notation *(this+0x30) for the slot link at 0x78 does not literally match the raw source's slot pointer derived from this+0x34; the ref is used verbatim as canonicalized evidence.
